clue.text: Desperate now SOS grows faint

indicators.note: desperate suggests frantic disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the distress call

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble sends a distress call and begins to pass out.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint or come close to fainting, here as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Go nuts when upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: bats and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy when they get upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, as in 'have a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means making an attempt, the same as having a go.

clue.text: Flower maiden falling for knight's nobility?

indicators.note: falling for here means losing its place to something else, so one letter gives way to another

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: London's river
M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A young woman falls in love with a knight, a romance of the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: THAMES loses its M and takes N in its place. 'Flower' is the classic crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanes were Scottish and Anglo-Saxon lords, so as a class they form a kind of nobility, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Accepting a bit of silver Judas set up King?

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
only a small part of the word is wanted, namely its opening letter
in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word is written upwards

blocks.note: Judas the betrayer; a rat is a traitor
first letter of silver

explanation.surface: Judas takes his thirty pieces of silver and betrays the King of the Jews.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, a monarch, so 'King?' is a loose example with a question mark.

clue.text: One distributing crap odds and who's opened a book?

blocks.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the off
someone who opens a book to read it

explanation.surface: A bookmaker who has opened a book offers lousy odds on a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened a book' and 'odds' paint a bookie, but the book is for reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A muck spreader is the farm machine that scatters manure across fields.

clue.text: One who's paid for playing power?

definitions.text: One who's paid for playing power?

blocks.note: a professional is paid to play
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman is paid for his physical strength.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a prop is a rugby forward, a professional prized for scrummaging power.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a prop is a front-row forward whose job is pushing strength in the scrum.

clue.text: Soviet consort beginning to belt out warning

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is wanted, just its opening letter
out means removed, so that letter is taken away from the consort

blocks.note: Reds was the common name for Soviet communists
Prince Albert, consort of Queen Victoria
first letter of belt

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader's spouse starts belting out a song of warning.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBERT loses the B, leaving ALERT. Albert is the best-known royal consort, husband of Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of readiness, an urgent signal of imminent danger.

clue.text: First of three hags moves jerkily

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: first letter of three
hags are ugly old witches

explanation.surface: The leading one of Macbeth's three witches twitches as she moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitching is making small sudden spasmodic movements, so it describes jerky motion.

clue.text: Cook's left Endeavour exhausted - it's dark and often bitter

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so the middle goes and only the two ends of the word remain

blocks.note: on a ship such as Captain Cook's, the left side is port
outer letters of Endeavour

explanation.surface: Captain Cook leaves his ship Endeavour worn out and craves a dark, bitter drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour was Cook's ship, which makes 'left' nautical.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer brewed with roasted malt, typically with a bitter taste.

clue.text: Space making way for genesis of baby in ladies?

definitions.text: Space making way for genesis of baby in ladies?

indicators.note: making way for means stepping aside so something else takes the spot
the genesis of a word is its beginning, so just its first letter

blocks.note: ladies are women
an en is a printer's space
first letter of baby

explanation.surface: A cryptic description of the place in women where babies begin.
explanation.walkthrough: In WOMEN the EN gives way to B. Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: the space in women where a baby begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The uterus is the organ in which a baby is conceived and grows before birth.

clue.text: Way of feeling balls

blocks.note: first meaning: a fibre carrying sensation through the body
second meaning: courage, slangily

explanation.surface: A cheeky phrase hinting at touching a sensitive part.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve is the pathway carrying sensation, and nerve is also boldness or guts.

clue.text: Take part in lap dancing lady's finale

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so the word is rearranged
a finale is the end, so only the closing letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of lady

explanation.surface: A woman joins in a lap dance as the show reaches its climax.
explanation.definitionFit: To play in a game or event is to participate, a direct synonym for taking part in.

clue.text: Special forces error tracking arsenic killer

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so these pieces come after the other one

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces
a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers mistakenly follow a trail of poison to find a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is someone who murders a prominent person, often for pay or politics.

clue.text: Behave badly and do lines at university

blocks.note: an actor does lines
being up is the British idiom for being at university, especially Oxbridge

explanation.surface: A student misbehaves and does lines of cocaine on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or show off, typically used of children or machines.

clue.text: Book of verse to be wrapped by Christmas

indicators.note: something wrapped by another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A poetry book will be gift-wrapped in time for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long work of prose fiction, published as a book.

clue.text: Doctor replacing edges of worn knife

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper, and here the tampering just swaps the end letters with each other

blocks.note: worn clothing is ragged

explanation.surface: A doctor swaps the blade on a blunt surgical knife.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first and last letters of RAGGED gives DAGGER. 'Doctor' looks like a physician, but it is the instruction to tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger is a short pointed blade used for stabbing, a kind of knife.

clue.text: A place to rest finally following good, all-night party

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second piece is put behind the first

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rave is a big dance party running through the night

explanation.surface: After a good all-night party, someone finally finds somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest finally' suggests sleeping after the party, but it means the last rest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is where the dead are buried, their resting place at the end of life.

clue.text: National run lacking heart

indicators.note: lacking its heart means the central letter is removed

blocks.note: to scoot is to run off quickly

explanation.surface: A national team's run of results lacks spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOOT loses its middle O. 'National' is used as a noun: a citizen of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, so a citizen or national of that country.

clue.text: Revealing parts of underwear use a catch from below to provide breathtaking opportunities?

indicators.note: revealing parts means the letters are on show inside the next few words
in a down clue, read from below means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Skimpy underwear with a catch underneath offers some breathtaking views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathtaking' looks like stunning, but it means literally taking a breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesurae are pauses within lines of verse, natural points for a reader to take a breath.

clue.text: Republican after new First Lady? Surely not!

indicators.note: after means placed later, so this piece follows the others

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Eve, the first woman in Genesis
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican is succeeded by a new First Lady, to general disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests the president's wife; here it is the Bible's first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Never as an exclamation expresses shocked disbelief, the same as saying surely that cannot be.

clue.text: Jotter from Spooner's craft corner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

blocks.note: a craft is a vessel, and a corner is a nook

explanation.surface: A notepad from the arts-and-crafts corner of a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests handicrafts, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small book of paper for notes, so a notebook.

clue.text: Trumps expressing loudly the workings of humanity?

indicators.note: expressing something out loud means the sound matters, here with the h dropped

blocks.note: hearts can be the trump suit in card games, said with a dropped h

explanation.surface: A question about what the inner workings of humanity are.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the h, as a Cockney does, is a common sound trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The arts, or humanities, cover what human beings make and think: literature, music and painting.

clue.text: Maybe Macbeth and Lady Macbeth tried to do it while sleeping?

definitions.text: Lady Macbeth tried to do it while sleeping

blocks.note: first meaning: a tyrannical ruler, as Macbeth became

blocks.clueFragment: Lady Macbeth tried to do it while sleeping
blocks.note: second meaning: in her sleepwalking scene she cries 'Out, damned spot!', trying to clean her hands

explanation.surface: Macbeth and his wife plotting murder in the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DE-SPOT: removing a spot, which is what Lady Macbeth tries to do while sleepwalking.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler wielding power cruelly, which Macbeth became after killing Duncan.

clue.text: Unresolved issue is eased after moving back north

indicators.note: moving the north letter further back rearranges the word by shifting one letter

blocks.note: eased off means loosened

explanation.surface: An outstanding problem is relieved after a move back up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The N, the abbreviation for north, moves one place back in LOOSENED.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail still to be settled or tied up, an outstanding matter.

clue.text: Where one might see matinee idol very high on cocaine

indicators.note: someone high on drugs is scrambled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A film star idol caught very high on cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matinee idol' reads as one phrase, but matinee belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Vic is a famous London theatre, a place to watch an afternoon performance.

clue.text: One no longer invested in stud supply

indicators.note: supply is read as an adverb, supplely, so the letters bend into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor pulls out of a horse-breeding stud business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial, but it means clothed, as in vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes without clothes, so is someone no longer dressed or clad.

clue.text: Ground fruit I set aside on the counter

indicators.note: setting aside means putting to one side, so that single letter is dropped
counter means running against, so the word is read the opposite way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some ground fruit has been put to one side on the kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like crushed, but it is the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is grass-covered earth, the ground of a racecourse or playing field.

clue.text: Note Queen's typical queries

blocks.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
Q is the abbreviation for Queen, plus the S

explanation.surface: A memo about the questions the Queen usually asks.
explanation.definitionFit: FAQs are frequently asked questions, the usual queries people raise about something.

clue.text: John in bed evacuated bodily fluid

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
evacuated means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word remain

blocks.note: outer letters of bed
john is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A patient named John, bedbound, has an accident with his bowels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood is the red liquid circulating through the veins, a fluid of the body.

clue.text: Books about American exile

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Memoirs about an American who has been banished.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to expel or drive out, the same as exiling someone, both as verbs.

clue.text: Son packing daughter's trunk

indicators.note: packing means stuffing into, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: a son is a boy
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A boy fills his sister's travel chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage; here it is the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the main part of the human body, the torso without head or limbs.

clue.text: Some scrub at home to get cleaner?

definitions.text: Some scrub at home to get cleaner?

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Some people scrub themselves at home to get clean.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: what you might use at home to get cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a tub of water used for washing the whole body clean.

clue.text: Ghost essentially taking oddly vacated seat in feast?

definitions.text: Ghost essentially taking oddly vacated seat in feast?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very centre, so the middle letter is wanted
taking a place means occupying it in place of something else
with the odd letters vacated, only the even letters are left

blocks.note: middle letter of ghost
second and fourth letters of seat
a banquet is a feast

explanation.surface: At Macbeth's banquet a ghost takes the empty seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue tells the story: the murdered Banquo's ghost sits in Macbeth's place at the feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo is the Shakespeare character whose spectre appears at the dinner table in Macbeth.

clue.text: Liable to take off clothes assuming good man is hot

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, here taking the clothes inside

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
kit is a set of clothing
taken as written
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A stripper keen to undress because a good man finds them hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off clothes' suggests stripping, but the definition stops at 'take off', as a nervous horse bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittish horse is nervous and easily startled, likely to bolt suddenly.
